threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting in a line for brunch on a Saturday is normal. We've already learned the real spots have no lines, mate.
Caught a bloke on the 3 bus singing opera at 2AM, while a group of teens tried to outdo him with rap. Pure Brixton chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted a Turkish man arguing passionately with a pigeon over a kebab wrapper in Hasenheide park. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find a late-night kebab stand that doubles as an art gallery, showcasing local artists while you munch on döner at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their stance on burritos; they’ll debate the merits of La Taqueria vs. El Farolito for hours but won’t step into Chipotle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy serenading the 38 bus with an acoustic guitar yesterday. Made the whole ride feel like a scene from a quirky indie film.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think la Vila de Gràcia is just for parties, but most of us secretly love the quiet streets after 10 PM. That’s when the real magic happens.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the hours some shops close, especially when they show up at 3 PM thinking they’ll grab a quick lunch.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare in awe at brunch menus longer than an episode of EastEnders, trying to decipher what 'avocado toast' really means.
Last night on the 59, a guy debated whether to eat his cold kebab or save it for breakfast—total silence until he said, 'It's a hero, not a zero.'

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the guy at the corner bakery bargaining with the cashier over a stale croissant, I knew I was truly embedded in Neukölln's vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a nightclub in an old public bathhouse, complete with mosaics and a sauna. Party while surrounded by history!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for the overpriced tacos at that touristy spot on 24th—real ones know La Taqueria never disappoints.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to fix his shattered phone screen with duct tape on the 38. Classic Tenderloin moment, and it somehow felt right.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but many locals avoid them on weekends—too crowded with selfie sticks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their baffled look as they try to figure out the ‘no honking’ rule on Carrer de Verdi during brunch hours.
